name: phot-o-matic
description: phot-o-MATIC — on-device footage triage for photographers. Scans video on Apple silicon with a whole-frame luminance-rise detector and an on-device Vision classifier, and returns candidate frames with their measurements and a written thumbnail. Ships an MCP server; requires macOS 26 on arm64.

metadata.compatibilityTier: MCP-host-full-operation ONLY, AND macOS 26 or later on Apple silicon (arm64) ONLY — this plugin ships a native Mach-O binary, not a script
metadata.requiresForFullOperation: a host able to launch stdio MCP servers, running macOS 26+ on arm64. There is no Intel build and no non-Apple port: the engine links Vision, CoreML and AVFoundation directly, which is the whole reason the classification runs on-device and costs no tokens.
metadata.note: THIS PHASE SHIPS THE ENGINE AND NO JUDGMENT. The coaching verdict is rendered from a criteria set, and no criteria set is bundled here. Until one is, every scan returns coaching.available=false together with the reason and the paths searched — read that field rather than inferring a verdict, and do not substitute one. A criteria set installed at ~/Library/Application Support/Walk/criteria.json, or named in WALK_CRITERIA, is loaded and rendered from; that path and that variable are unchanged on purpose, so an installed set does not go dark when the product is named. Hosts that omit mcpServers plugins will not install this pack, and hosts below the macOS/arch floor get a server that advertises zero tools and states the reason rather than failing silently. The six MCP tool names are still walk_* : Walk was the development name, the tool names are the stable API, and they deliberately did not move.
